Increased 5‐l-oxoxygenase activity in a rat liver injury model correlates with the number of infiltrating neutrophil granulocytes.
5‐lOx activity in the injured liver is attributable to neutrophilic infiltration.
1) 5‐LO activity was markedly increased in massive hepatic necrosis, 2) 5‐lpoxygenase activity was detected in neutrophils, and 3) neutrophils were infiltrated in the necrotic livers.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the role of the neutrophils and their products in liver injury.
the study of the effects of various chemical compounds, including drugs, on the metabolism of the liver, and the mechanisms by which these compounds exert their toxic effects on the liver.
the role of neutrophils in the development of massive liver necrosis induced by P. acnes and lipopolysacaccharide.

neutrophils are not the only source of the increased 5-lipoxygenase activity.
